$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector ![](images/9e/9e7b8bc888dbf7a764c0d5b9533758277b59e78d476a3cfe7bbfb2fcac7e7363.svg)

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 2+6\cdot 4+4\cdot (-4)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-2+24-16|}{\sqrt{4+16+16}} \\  & =\frac{|\,6\,|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119840 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-072e9e45-d148-5a1a-9029-08725d744a80" "question-ee5f2c99-4524-5cc2-872a-3bdd6d04d82a"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119841 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-152abe46-196c-57ed-801a-b01b3b6e9019"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-c2de4bc9-44ca-5148-a12b-218413513154" :question/id #uuid "c2de4bc9-44ca-5148-a12b-218413513154" :question/math-academy-id "q-34071" :question/problem "Find the shortest distance between the point $P(1,1,-1)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-⟨3,0,1⟩)\cdot ⟨1,-8,4⟩=0.$" :question/worked-solution "Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(3,0,1).$ Then

$$
z=9+3(1)-(1)=11.

$$

"question-152abe46-196c-57ed-801a-b01b3b6e9019" :question/id #uuid "152abe46-196c-57ed-801a-b01b3b6e9019" :question/math-academy-id "q-34033" :question/problem "Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-1,0,2)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $2x-y+2z=-1.$" :question/worked-solution "Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=2$ and $y=3$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y+2z & =-1 \\ 2(2)-(3)+2z & =-1 \\ 2z & =-2 \\ z & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(2,3,-1)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,3,-1⟩-⟨-1,0,2⟩ \\  & =⟨3,3,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨2,-1,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|3\cdot 2+3\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|6-3-6|}{\sqrt{4+1+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,-3\,|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-4a75b517-d88b-5fde-8c47-3acf225f13a9"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-4a75b517-d88b-5fde-8c47-3acf225f13a9" :answer-field/id #uuid "4a75b517-d88b-5fde-8c47-3acf225f13a9" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-a40f70a0-ef1e-59d6-9c75-8bb1b576296f" :answer-field/choices ["answer-66952a23-b25c-549f-a606-5d6dda11f34c" "answer-a40f70a0-ef1e-59d6-9c75-8bb1b576296f" "answer-1d85d58b-d2c6-50e6-b647-b9ac50af4bb1" "answer-5ad1e3d5-d1ee-5ca4-bb25-a289369682c6" "answer-75964f2d-1d14-5218-b72a-c985ff68e537"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-66952a23-b25c-549f-a606-5d6dda11f34c" :answer/id #uuid "66952a23-b25c-549f-a606-5d6dda11f34c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a40f70a0-ef1e-59d6-9c75-8bb1b576296f" :answer/id #uuid "a40f70a0-ef1e-59d6-9c75-8bb1b576296f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1d85d58b-d2c6-50e6-b647-b9ac50af4bb1" :answer/id #uuid "1d85d58b-d2c6-50e6-b647-b9ac50af4bb1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\sqrt{6}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5ad1e3d5-d1ee-5ca4-bb25-a289369682c6" :answer/id #uuid "5ad1e3d5-d1ee-5ca4-bb25-a289369682c6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-75964f2d-1d14-5218-b72a-c985ff68e537" :answer/id #uuid "75964f2d-1d14-5218-b72a-c985ff68e537" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120020 :activity/expected-seconds 960.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y+2z & =-1 \\ 2(2)-(3)+2z & =-1 \\ 2z & =-2 \\ z & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(2,3,-1)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,3,-1⟩-⟨-1,0,2⟩ \\  & =⟨3,3,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|3\cdot 2+3\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|6-3-6|}{\sqrt{4+1+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,-3\,|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-8y+8z & =-36 \\ 4(-1)-8(1)+8z & =-36 \\ 8z & =-24 \\ z & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-1,1,-3)$ which lies on the plane.

$$

[{:db/id 17592186120724 :step/content {:db/id 17592186121054 :tutorial/content "Suppose we want to find the shortest distance between the point $P(3,0,-2)$ and the plane $\Pi$ that is given by the equation 

$$
(\mathbf{r}-\langle 2 , 3 , 1 \rangle ) \cdot \langle 4 , 4 , 2 \rangle = 0.
$$

 

First, note that $\mathbf{n} = \langle 4 , 4 , 2 \rangle$ is a vector that's normal to the plane.

![](images/7b/7b2dfcd87c1f5e4e2c2b1a0b9a7f73899772e33e1020465b2b38d1b2de29a66c.png)

Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(2,3,1)$. Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,3,1⟩-⟨3,0,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,3,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The shortest distance $d$ from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane, as shown below.

![](images/26/26e494eef47db4dba3ac36dfa96c7e9a9d191321b22bb82874f3e74bbd7116ef.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 4+3\cdot 4+3\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-4+12+6|}{\sqrt{16+16+4}} \\  & =\frac{|14|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is $\dfrac{7}{3}.$" :tutorial/id #uuid "224c4104-9097-5a92-9c37-5d0fe22171a6" :tutorial/math-academy-id 3261 $$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,3,1⟩-⟨3,0,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,3,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The shortest distance $d$ from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane, as shown below.

![](images/26/26e494eef47db4dba3ac36dfa96c7e9a9d191321b22bb82874f3e74bbd7116ef.png)

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 4+3\cdot 4+3\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-4+12+6|}{\sqrt{16+16+4}} \\  & =\frac{|14|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
